sense: a talent, a skill, a plan

terms.comment: Of people, minds and talents: to train and refine them.

evidence: Cic. Cael. 45: ingenium industriā alitur (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Off. 1.105: hominis autem mēns discendō alitur et cōgitandō
terms.comment: A talent grows on what feeds it.
Of a new plan, method or thing: to develop a recipe, a game, a program.

phrases.latin: prōtinus excolimur tenerī cūrāque parentis īmus ad īnsignēs urbis ab arte virōs
phrases.english: from our earliest years we were schooled, and by our father’s care we went to the men of the city famous for their art

phrases.latin: hominis autem mēns discendō alitur et cōgitandō
phrases.english: the human mind is fed by learning and thinking

phrases.latin: cum recentī fīcō salis vice cāseō vescī nūper excōgitātum est
phrases.english: eating cheese with fresh figs instead of salt is a recent invention

sources: Lewis & Short: excolo · Lewis & Short: alo · Lewis & Short: excogito
